records.title: Attack 1 · AK

fields.narrative: fired three torpedo spread at range of 1,800 yards, track of 85° port, depth setting 12 feet, and gyro angle of 355°. Results one hit, one miss, and one premature. From checking times of firing and explosions, it was concluded that the first torpedo hit amidships, the second torpedo prematured at 23 seconds, and the third torpedo seemed to miss astern. The terrific explosion and turbulence produced by the premature may have thrown the third torpedo off its track as it swerved off to the right. All torpedoes were spread to hit the target as our information had checked accurately. Although disconcerting, the premature proved helpful in providing a smoke and water screen of about 100 feet height behind which we turned away. We cleared this screen just in time to observe a torpedo hit amidships. This hit was followed shortly by a flash of flame and an explosion aboard the target distinct from the hit. The target began to fire bow and stern guns of about 5" caliber toward our firing position which we had rapidly left astern. This target was the largest ship this vessel has fired at to date. He was well over 500 feet in length. His silhouette and upper works as seen during the daytime showed him to be similar to the Husimi Maru, 10,800 tons, page 33 of ONI-208-J. After the hit, the pip on the radar seemed to decrease about 1/3 and then stay the same size. We opened range to 7,500 yards and then rounded target to attack again from northward should he fail to sink. Target continued to fire guns to southward for about twenty minutes. Then numerous lights were seen about the decks.

fields.event: fired three torpedo spreads at range of 1,300 yards, 37° starboard track, 0° gyro angle, and depth setting of 15 feet. Results Nos. 1 and 2 prematured at 23 seconds; No. 3 hit target in bow. It is believed that targed slowed down on seeing prematures as #3 should have hit aft. When first two torpedoes prematured, made three more tubes ready for firing.

records.title: Attack on Taigen Maru type AK (No. 4 torpedo)

fields.event: fired #4 torpedo at range of 1,700 yards with a track of 161° starboard, and 001° gyro angle. Torpedo missed as target evaded. Target took a 30° down angle, raised his screw partly out of the water, gave us a 180° angle on bow, and pulled away at about 8 knots. The target fired about 30 rounds from his stern gun at the periscope.

flags: Gyro angle printed 001° (Gemini read 00°). Target fired about 30 rounds at the periscope.

fields.event: [SUMMARY] Surfaced at 16,000 yards range to commence surface chase, but target had more speed than expected and Finback did not gain bearing rapidly.

abandoned chase when we reached 72 feet of water and he was still bearing 245° (T). It was heart breaking to lose an unescorted target with such a perfect set up. This retirement proved to be none to soon.

records.title: Attack 3 · AK

fields.narrative: with escort at 2,000 yards, fired three torpedo spreads from bow tubes with following setup: track angle 95° (S); range 1,700 yards; gyro angle 4° right; and depth setting of 12 feet. All torpedoes seemed to run normally and looked good. Results - No hits. With the spreads used, the consistency of our data, and actual torpedo tracks observed, the commanding officer believes it was impossible to get three misses unless the torpedoes ran too deep. A subsequent careful check-up of all personnel and data has not revealed any explanation for three misses. When the third torpedo left the tube, swung ship hard right at flank speed and placed target astern.

records.title: Attack 4 · AK

fields.narrative: fired two torpedoes from after tubes by applying lead angle on after T.D.T. and using zero gyro angles. Results two hits. The first torpedo hit amidships giving off a large amount of flame. The second torpedo hit well aft. The target was covered with black smoke, but seemed to start down aft at once. All hands on bridge watched bow rise out of water and then the target took its final plunge. At the same time the radar officer watched his pip increase and then disappear. The target sank in two and one-half minutes. Apparently neither the target, who was closed to 1,300 yards, nor the escort who closed us to 2,400 yards, with a broadsideview, ever saw us. The escort charged off astern of target dropping depth charges to a total of nine. They sound fine when you are on the surface. Cleared area to north, got off message to CTF 71.1, and headed east so as to be able to clear area the next night.

records.title: Attack 5 · AK

fields.narrative: fired a three torpedo spread from stern tubes with 90° port track, 2,000 yard range, 180° gyro angle, and 12 foot depth setting. Results first torpedo hit under stack, second and third torpedoes missed ahead and astern as they should have, since a spread of 125% coverage was used. The target was very lightly loaded and riding high. It was identified as the Tatumiya Maru, 6,344 tons, page 77 of ONI-208-J. Changed course 90° to left after watching torpedo hit, to clear torpedo track. Although escort was hard to make out, sound heard him speed up immediately following the torpedo explosion. Ran at full speed for ten minutes and went deep.

records.title: Attack 7 · AK

fields.narrative: fired two bow tubes at 3,900 yard range, 0° gyro angle, 90° starboard track, and spread torpedoes by using masts as points of aim. Results two misses astern. The target seemed to kick ahead very slowly just as we fired. We had used a target speed of zero. This time the target opened up with his gun. No splashes were seen. This failure meant that our next attack would have to be a submerged one in daylight as dawn had begun breaking in the east.

records.title: Gunfire from patrol vessel

fields.event: just as ship was turning northward to patrol the following day off Pomalaa, Celebes, picked up target on radar at 3,750 yards, 034° relative. At that time we sighted a patrol vessel visually for the first time and turned away. When the commanding officer arrived on the bridge, he found a patrol vessel with a big bow wave bearing down with zero angle on the bow and range of 2,700 yards. The range opened fairly rapidly as four Fairbanks-Morse engines warmed up. At a range of about 3,500 yards, the patrol vessel presented a 10° angle on the bow and opened fired with a gun of about 3" caliber. At this point the FINBACK joined the group that strongly believes in the 5" gun aft. Decided to stay on surface as long as we opened range and firing was not too accurate. The only close shot dropped 75 yards to starboard of forward engine room hatch. This shot did not explode. He continued to fire until range opened to 6,000 yards. As he was in our path to Pomalaa, decided to retire to southeast and patrol southwest of Buton Island the following day. This patrol vessel was only seen head on. At first he appeared to be a small destroyer, but as he only made about 10-11 knots it is believed that he was a PC type patrol boat.

records.title: Gun action off Boeroe Island

fields.event: surfaced and started in pursuit. The range to the steamer by SJ radar was 9,000 yards. This showed we had been farther off the beach. Closed targets at full speed on the surface. They paid no attention until we opened fired on the steamer at 5,000 yards range. The steamer was light and very high out of the water. Hit steamer about five times. Leading mine planter turned toward us and opened fire with a gun which seemed to be about a one pounder. Directed 4" fire at this ship. He continued to close range in spite of numerous hits until we opened fire with our three 20 mm guns and two 50 caliber machine guns. This barrage combined with a fire breaking out on board, discouraged him and he opened range rapidly. This vessel had settled about three feet. Shifted fire back to the steamer and the second mine planter began closing us. His machine gun fire was falling about 100 yards short. Began to hit him repeatedly with 4" gun. Soon put him on fire from stem to stern. He finally headed for the beach blazing furiously. At this point the first mine planter began to fire at a range of about 8,000 yards. Shifted fire to steamer again and obtained about five more hits. When the mine planter began to straddle us at 6,500 yards, decided the one pounder had gotten larger, and as we had only twenty rounds of 4" left, retired to westward. The mine planters were from 500 1,000 tons. Pictures obtained may provide a better estimate. The one set on fire sank enroute to the beach. The damaged ships headed eastward with power plants apparently intact. Expended 100 rounds of 4" ammunition. As we had been along normal traffic lanes from Ambon to Tioro Strait and Makassar for several days without results, decided to work north of Ceram following day hunting for traffic to Dampier Strait and Babo, New Guinea. Following that, planned to concentrate on Dampier Strait which is reported virgin territory with some traffic.

records.title: Attack 8 · AK

fields.narrative: fired two torpedo spread from bow tubes at 1,430 yards range with 113 starboard track, 028° gyro angle, and depth setting of 12 feet. Results - two misses. Swung ship hard right; Just as we were going to fire our stern tubes, noticed backing wash from target's screws. While shifting set up, target turned away giving us a large angle on the bow. Decided not to throw away any torpedoes. The escort apparently did not see us. The target must have seen us just prior to firing or after we started turning. The torpedoes ran normally and our set-up had checked accurately. The torpedo tracks looked good. Unless we were discovered at firing point, at least one torpedo should have hit. Our only mistake was that in trying to keep a small silhouette to both target and escort, a 028° right gyro was accepted. Target and escort headed south as we opened to north. Escort dropped two depth charges aimlessly. Abandoned chase as we could not get ahead of target undetected before he began to hug coast of Ceram. At daylight, he could be in either Kelang or Manipa Strait. This set-up had checked so accurately that we had already credited ourselves with 5,000 tons.

fields.event: made radar contact on object at 5,400 yards bearing 037° relative. Unable to sight object. Decided to exchange identification signals. Found ship was TAMBOR. First sighted TAMBOR from astern at 1,900 yards. She fell in astern and took up our speed.
